title: High-Credibility Specialist & Beat Publications
description: Domain-dedicated newsrooms and analytical publications whose reporters and editors possess deep technical, scientific, legal, or defense literacy.

sources.name: STAT News
sources.ownership_and_funding: Privately owned by Boston Globe Media Partners (John W. Henry); editorially independent biomedical newsroom.
sources.editorial_standards: Specialized medical/clinical trial scrutiny; reporters examine primary FDA briefing documents, trial endpoints, p-hacking, and statistical power rather than press releases.
strengths: Premier scrutiny of clinical trial results, vaccine/outbreak epidemiology, FDA advisory panels, and biopharma claims
Rapidly identifies methodological flaws in hyped medical press releases
known_limitations_and_biases: U.S. FDA/NIH regulatory ecosystem emphasis compared to EMA or Asian regulators
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Pair STAT reporting with the underlying ClinicalTrials.gov registry, PubMed peer-reviewed study, or WHO/CDC surveillance data.

sources.name: Nature News (Journalism Division)
sources.ownership_and_funding: Published by Springer Nature; the News & Comment team is editorially independent of Nature's journal peer-review editors.
sources.editorial_standards: Solicits independent outside domain-scientist commentary on every reported study or preprint, explicitly flagging sample size, replication risks, and unrefereed status.
strengths: Translates frontier discoveries in physics, biology, climate, AI, and spaceflight without sensationalizing preprints
Investigative coverage of research misconduct, paper mills, and global science funding policy
known_limitations_and_biases: Focuses on academic research developments rather than operational field logistics
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Always trace the DOI cited in Nature News back to the primary paper and check independent replication commentary.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.editorial_standards: Subject-matter beat writers (aerospace, semiconductor architecture, patent/antitrust dockets, security engineering) linking directly to primary filings and specs.
strengths: Technically accurate explanations of CPU/GPU architectures, spaceflight telemetry, tech antitrust court filings, and AI benchmarks
Consistent linking to primary dockets, RFCs, and technical white papers
known_limitations_and_biases: Occasional conversational editorial tone; distinguish deep-dive technical reporting from quick-turn aggregated posts
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Verify technical specifications against NIST/IETF/vendor datasheets or court filings cited in the article.

sources.name: KrebsOnSecurity
sources.ownership_and_funding: Independent investigative cybersecurity publication by former Washington Post reporter Brian Krebs; ad-supported with transparent disclosures.
sources.editorial_standards: Primary forensic OSINT on DNS records, dark-web forums, blockchain flows, and corporate breach artifacts prior to publication.
strengths: Deep investigative attribution of cybercrime syndicates, data breaches, identity-broker ecosystems, and banking fraud
Publishes technical indicators and documentary evidence
known_limitations_and_biases: Single-investigator newsroom bandwidth means selective high-impact investigations rather than comprehensive daily CVE tracking
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Pair breach reporting with CISA/NVD advisories, SEC 8-K Item 1.05 cybersecurity disclosures, and The Record.

sources.name: The Record (by Recorded Future News)
sources.ownership_and_funding: Published by Recorded Future (threat intelligence firm, acquired by Mastercard) with an explicit editorial independence charter for its journalism staff.
sources.editorial_standards: Dedicated beat reporters covering nation-state APTs, ransomware attacks on critical infrastructure/municipalities, and global cyber norms.
strengths: Daily global reporting on ransomware, critical-infrastructure intrusions, telecom espionage, and cyber diplomacy
Direct on-the-record interviews with national cyber directors and CERT leaders
known_limitations_and_biases: Parent-company proximity to the commercial threat-intelligence industry—always distinguish attributed CERT/government advisories from single-vendor threat marketing
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Cross-check APT attribution claims across multiple independent threat-intel vendors and national CERT/CISA advisories.

sources.name: Lawfare
sources.ownership_and_funding: Published by The Lawfare Institute (501(c)(3) non-profit) in cooperation with Brookings; transparent donor list.
sources.editorial_standards: Edited legal analysis and primary courtroom/docket reporting written by legal scholars, former national security counsel, and credentialed court reporters.
strengths: Granular statutory, constitutional, international humanitarian law (LOAC/IHL), sanctions law, and AI-governance analysis
Curates primary indictments, judicial orders, and executive orders
known_limitations_and_biases: Reflects mainstream U.S. institutional national-security-law establishment perspectives; normative legal interpretations can be contested among scholars
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Separate Lawfare's primary docket summaries from interpretive legal arguments; pair contested legal questions with SCOTUSblog, ICJ filings, and comparative legal scholarship.

sources.name: SCOTUSblog
sources.ownership_and_funding: Independent appellate law news and docket archive; sponsor-disclosed.
sources.editorial_standards: Hosts complete case files (petitions, merits briefs, amici, oral argument transcripts, slip opinions) alongside neutral procedural explainers.
strengths: Definitive procedural tracking and plain-English doctrinal breakdown of U.S. Supreme Court litigation
Direct links to every party and amicus brief
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Read the linked slip opinion, dissent, and statutory text directly to verify exact holding boundaries.

sources.name: Carbon Brief
sources.ownership_and_funding: UK-based non-profit publication funded by philanthropic climate/science foundations (European Climate Foundation, etc.) with editorial independence.
sources.editorial_standards: Science-first data journalism: every factual claim links to peer-reviewed literature, IPCC chapters, or national grid/customs datasets.
strengths: Unmatched quantitative breakdowns of national emissions trajectories (especially China, EU, US, India), COP negotiations, grid economics, and extreme-weather attribution
Clear methodological appendices explaining climate models and uncertainty ranges
known_limitations_and_biases: Philanthropic climate-foundation funding means strong focus on decarbonization pathways—verify industrial/grid cost assumptions against IEA, EIA, and peer-reviewed energy economics
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Cross-check emissions and energy-mix data with IPCC, NOAA/Copernicus, and primary national energy statistics.

sources.name: War on the Rocks
sources.ownership_and_funding: Published by Metamorphic Media LLC; subscription and sponsorship funded.
sources.editorial_standards: Peer-edited operational and strategic defense analysis authored by military practitioners, defense economists, and conflict scholars.
strengths: Explains military logistics, force generation, air-defense attrition, naval warfare, and deterrence mechanics far more accurately than generalist cable news
Counters sensationalist 'wunderwaffe' or instant-collapse tropes in active wars
known_limitations_and_biases: Primarily analytical commentary rather than primary battlefield wire reporting; individual authors hold distinct strategic schools of thought (restraint vs. primacy)
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Use for operational/doctrinal mechanics and pair with Bellingcat/CIR geo-verified ground data and SIPRI/IISS force baselines.

sources.name: Foreign Affairs
sources.ownership_and_funding: Published by the Council on Foreign Relations (non-partisan U.S. membership and research organization).
sources.editorial_standards: Rigorous editorial fact-checking of essays by leading international-relations scholars, historians, and sitting/former heads of state and diplomats.
strengths: Bridges current diplomatic crises with grand-strategy scholarship, economic statecraft theory, and historical analogies
Publishes competing strategic arguments side-by-side
known_limitations_and_biases: Essays argue strategic theses (treat as expert analytical argument, not raw wire fact); sitting officials writing in Foreign Affairs are advancing state messaging
sources.corroboration_pairing_rule: Distinguish scholar-authored empirical essays from official-authored diplomatic signaling; pair with non-U.S. regional commentary.
